notes:
**Three findings that were wrong about somebody else's site.**

**The old "Tweet this" button is no longer called a broken link.** X answers a
crawler with 404 for both forms of its share URL — `/intent/tweet` and the older
`/share` — while returning 200 to a browser. Version 1.3.25 excluded the first
and missed the second, so any theme still using the older button had it reported
as a dead outbound link. Both are excluded now, matched on a whole path segment,
so a real account whose name merely begins with "share" is still checked.

**"When it comes to" is no longer treated as a sign of AI-written copy.** It was
on the list of phrases that mark unedited machine output, and it is ordinary
English. Measured across 660 pages of three human-written institutional sites, it
appeared on 19 of them and every other phrase on the list appeared on none.
Because two phrases are needed to trigger the finding, this one turned a single
genuine cliché into a page reported as "generic AI-generated copy" with advice to
rewrite it. The real clichés still are.

**An hreflang tag pointing at the right page is no longer told to point
somewhere else.** Docket read "how the crawler arrived at this page" as "where
this page sends you", so a translation URL that another address redirects *to* —
exactly what the tag should name — was reported as redirecting, with advice to
point it at a destination it already was. Tags that genuinely redirect, 404 or
carry a noindex are still reported.
